title: Tables and Bulk Operations
intro: Complex tables and bulk import are the B2B work most products get wrong — and the import succeeds or fails in its repair step.

learn.title: Tables start from tasks
learn.text:
Work out which filters, sorts, search, editing modes and permissions are actually needed.

• Let users build their own filter set; consider per-column filters for speed
• Let users show, hide and reorder columns when comparison matters
• Offer compact and comfortable **density modes**
• Test with very long and very short values, and with pseudo-localisation
• Check how a screen reader moves through the table

options: Different users need different row counts on screen
It is required for WCAG compliance
It compensates for long translated strings
try.explain: Some users scan many rows; others read a few in detail.

learn.title: Row actions must be visible
learn.text:
**Avoid hover-only row actions.** They cause errors and rage clicks, they don't exist on touch, and keyboard users can't reach them predictably.

Use visible buttons on each row.

try.q: What does the note say about hover-reveal row actions?
options: They cause errors and rage clicks
They work if the hover area is large
They are acceptable on desktop-only tools
They should be paired with a tooltip

learn.title: Five stages of bulk import
learn.text:
**1. Pre-import** — template, example file, guardrails
**2. Upload** — drag, keyboard, copy-paste
**3. Map** — match columns, check values
**4. Repair** — show only the error rows; dedupe
**5. Import** — summary, and tag the new records

Most products dismiss a file as corrupt or invalid. **The value is in helping users fix it in place.**

try.q: Which stage decides whether a bulk import succeeds?
try.explain: Letting users fix mismatches inside the flow instead of rejecting the file.

test.q: What is the most common bulk-import failure?
options: Rejecting the file instead of helping fix it
test.explain: “Invalid file” ends the task; a repair step completes it.

test.q: What should the repair step show?
options: The full file with errors highlighted

test.q: When should users be able to reorder columns?
options: Whenever the table has more than five columns
When the table is printed or exported
test.explain: Along with showing and hiding them.

test.q: What should you test a table with?
options: Very long and very short values
test.explain: Plus pseudo-localisation, to catch layouts that break in translation.

test.q: What happens at the final import stage?
options: A summary, and the new records get tagged
The file is archived for audit
test.explain: Tagging lets users find what they just imported.
